title: How to change cursor in Apple Mail on Mac: a guide for system settings
metaTitle: How to Change Cursor on Mac: Apple Mail Guide
description: Learn how to change cursor on Mac to improve visibility. While Apple Mail does not have individual settings, you can adjust the pointer system-wide.
targetKeyword: how to change cursor on mac
intro: You cannot change the cursor specifically within the Apple Mail application as it uses the system-wide pointer style. To change the cursor on your Mac, you must adjust the settings in the macOS System Settings menu.
tldr: There is no per-app setting for the cursor in Apple Mail.
Changes to the cursor affect every application on your Mac.
Access these settings via System Settings > Accessibility > Display.
You can modify pointer size, outline color, and fill color.
Third-party apps are required for custom cursor shapes or animations.

blocks.text: Many users want to change their cursor to make it more visible while reading emails. macOS treats the cursor as a global element. This means any change you make applies to Apple Mail, Safari, and every other window you open. The operating system does not offer a way to set a unique cursor for specific apps.
How to Change Cursor on Mac System Settings
The following steps work for macOS Ventura, Sonoma, and Sequoia. These settings are designed to help users with visual impairments or those working on high resolution displays.

items: Click the Apple menu () in the top menu bar.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click on Accessibility in the left sidebar.
Select the Display option from the list of features.
Scroll down until you see the Pointer section.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preferred width.
Click the Pointer outline color box to pick a new border.
Click the Pointer fill color box to change the center color.

blocks.text: Using the Shake to Locate Feature

If you often lose track of your cursor while working in a busy inbox, the shake feature is a helpful alternative. When you move your mouse or trackpad quickly, the cursor grows in size for a second. This makes it instantly visible against a wall of text. You can toggle this on in the same Accessibility menu under the Pointer section.
Third Party Tools for Custom Cursors

If you want to use custom shapes, like a different icon or an animated cursor, native macOS settings will not suffice. You must look into third party software. Tools like Mousecape or Cursor Craft allow you to replace system pointer files. Note that these apps modify system files. Always check the security settings in System Settings > Privacy & Security if your Mac blocks them from running.

Sometimes changes do not take effect immediately. Try restarting your Mac if the cursor size does not update. If you use a third party app and want to revert to the default look, use the Reset or Restore Default option within that specific app. Do not try to manually delete system cursor files as this can cause instability.
Why Apple Mail Does Not Have Cursor Settings

Apple maintains a consistent design language across its apps. By keeping cursor control at the system level, Apple ensures that all applications behave predictably. This prevents issues where a custom cursor might disappear or become invisible when hovering over specific interface elements like a search bar or a message preview.

Adjusting the pointer size or color via the native macOS settings has no measurable impact on your Mac performance. It is a simple UI change. Third party tools that add animations might consume a tiny amount of CPU resources, but this is usually negligible on modern Macs with Apple silicon. If you notice your Mac slowing down, check if your cursor app is running in the background.

High resolution displays, or Retina displays, pack many pixels into a small space. This can make the standard cursor look very small. Apple included these pointer adjustments specifically to solve this visibility problem. If you find yourself constantly squinting to find your cursor, increasing the size by just 10 percent can make a massive difference in your daily workflow.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor only for Apple Mail?
faq.answer: No, macOS does not support app-specific cursor settings. Any change you make in Accessibility settings will apply to every application on your Mac.

faq.question: How do I make my cursor bigger on a Mac?
faq.answer: Go to System Settings > Accessibility > Display and move the Pointer size slider to the right.

faq.question: Are there free apps to get custom cursors?
faq.answer: Yes, there are third-party tools like Mousecape, but be careful to download them from reputable sources and check your security settings.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor color slow down my Mac?
faq.answer: No, changing the cursor color or size through native system settings has no impact on your system performance.

task: Change the cursor appearance on your Mac system.
appliesTo: macOS Ventura, Sonoma, Sequoia, and later versions.
requirements: A Mac running macOS Ventura or later

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu () in the top left corner of your screen and select System Settings.

steps.name: Navigate to Accessibility
steps.text: Find and click Accessibility in the left sidebar menu.

steps.name: Open Display Settings
steps.text: Locate the Vision section and click on Display to manage your pointer settings.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer
steps.text: Scroll down to the Pointer section and use the sliders to change size or the color boxes to change the appearance.

troubleshooting.fix: Restart your Mac to ensure the system processes refresh the cursor theme.
Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security to allow the app to run.
